title: UMaine football ends season in a 24-21 loss to UNH - The Maine Campus
content: ORONO, Maine — On Saturday, Nov. 21, the University of Maine football team ended its season against the University of New Hampshire with a 24-21 loss. Maine came out strong with the first touchdown 10 minutes into the game from first-year wide receiver Ty Boone. Redshirt second-year kicker Samuel Tremblay completed the extra point to give the Black Bears seven points. They could not hold on to the lead for long, as UNH came back with a touchdown with four minutes left in the first quarter from graduate student running back Myles Thomason to tie it up. Maine was able to take back the lead with a deep pass from redshirt first-year quarterback Michale McMaugh to redshirt second-year running back Rashawn Marshall for a touchdown. Maine closed out the second quarter tied at 21-21 to enter halftime. In the third quarter, the score stayed the same with not much action. Going into the last quarter, the Wildcats got a field goal from second-year kicker Lucas Glassburn that secured the three winning points for UNH to win the game 24-21. This loss concluded Maine’s 2026 season with a disappointing 1-10 overall record. Maine lost 10 straight games, a program-record losing streak. The team’s only win came in the first game of the season, a 21-18 victory against Towson University, which created belief and hope for the rest of the season. Unfortunately, this was not the case, as Maine went on to lose 55-3 against Appalachian State University the next week and every game since. A unique moment in the season was the rotation of three different quarterbacks. In some games, the coaching staff would switch quarterbacks for every offensive play, which is almost never done in football. At the beginning of the season, redshirt second-year Eddie Buehler was the starting quarterback for the Black Bears after competing against redshirt third-year Caden Drezek in the preseason. Halfway through the regular season, when nothing was working offensively, the staff decided to mix things up and alternate between Buehler and Drezek for offensive plays. Drezek performed well under pressure and earned the starting quarterback position until the last two games, when McMaugh played full games as a third-string quarterback. Anybody can tell that Maine had offensive difficulties this entire season just by looking at the scores. The team tried to fix this problem by firing offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Mikahael Waters on Oct. 5, in the middle of the season, which is uncommon. Waters was replaced by running backs coach Sean Green. “Those are decisions that are really hard and affect everyone,” said head coach Jordan Stevens. “There’s a lot that goes into that to do what’s best for the football team and put us in a better position to win.” The Black Bears will have time to assess the season during the break and look to rebuild during the spring to hopefully come back with a better record next season. title: UNH football beats Maine on late field goal, retains Brice-Cowell Musket - Seacoastonline.com
content: ORONO, Maine – Sophomore Lucas Glassburn kicked the game-winning 44-yard field goal to lift the University of New Hampshire football team to Saturday afternoon’s 24-21 victory against the University of Maine at Alfond Stadium to retain the Brice-Cowell Musket, which is presented annually to the winner of this interstate rivalry game. UNH claimed the Musket for the fifth consecutive year, and the Wildcats have won 14 of the last 16 matchups and 21 of 24 dating back to the 2003 season. UNH sophomore quarterback Tommy McLeish completed 27 of 38 passes for 245 yards, including a 36-yard touchdown to grad student tight end Colby Ramshaw and an 11-yard TD to sophomore wide receiver Ryan Ricketti. Senior wide receiver Ja’Carree Kelly had eight catches for 65 yards, and Ramshaw finished with 48 yards on three receptions and Ricketti had five catches for 42 yards. Grad student Myles Thomason was UNH’s top rusher with 42 yards, and he also had a 39-yard punt return that set up a touchdown. The defensive unit was led by grad student safety Jackson Stone with nine tackles and sophomore linebackers Trevor Barry and Matthew Sopp with eight apiece. Maine was led offensively by Rashawn Marshall’s 164 rushing yards and Michael McMaugh’s three TD passes. Sam Oppenheier led all players with 12 tackles. UNH extended its season-ending win streak to three games to finish at 5-7 overall and 4-4 in the CAA. Maine lost its 10th consecutive game to finish 1-10 overall and 1-7 in the CAA. Late on Thursday, November 19, 2026, UnitedHealth Group (NYSE:UNH | UNH Price Prediction) sued the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) in federal court in Brunswick, Georgia. The suit challenges its 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings. The company alleges that CMS improperly used 26 measures to rate 45 of its contracts. It says the agency either lacked the legal authority to do so, gave the company no chance to object, or both. UnitedHealth says those contracts would score at least half a star and up to 1.5 stars higher if CMS calculated them correctly. The court has not ruled, and CMS declined to comment. The stock closed Friday, November 20, at $339.85, up 2.84%, while the S&P 500 fell 3.70%. That gain followed a 5.6% drop on Thursday, which came amid concerns about a proposed CMS audit crackdown and Medicare expansion plans. TD Cowen also upgraded the shares to Buy on Friday morning, so the lawsuit alone does not explain the move. In after-hours trading, the stock was at $335.50, down 1.35%, and that price can change before Monday’s open. CMS rates plans from 1 to 5 stars, and contracts with at least four stars earn government bonus payments. A half-star swing matters most for a contract sitting just under four stars, because crossing that line unlocks bonus money that pays for richer benefits and lower premiums. The complaint calls the ratings the government’s “principal signal” to patients about plan quality. It warns that low ratings could cut benefits and raise premiums. UnitedHealth said it did not take the step lightly and still wants to work with CMS on the Stars program. The company has disclosed no dollar figure for what it stands to lose.
